text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. President Bill Clinton, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu aim to restart peace.
- Jewish settler from Dolev shoots two Palestinians after his car is stoned.
- Bezeq Communications share offer approval delayed over workers' rights.
- First phase of Discount share offer successful.
- Eli Lilly, the Indianapolis-based pharmaceutical company, to open Tel Aviv subsidiary.
GLOBES
- Prime minister to convene meeting on Sunday with Finance Minister Dan Meridor, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel on joint effort to achieve swift growth.
- Dollar reaches record 3.381 shekels.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu after meeting Clinton: Building on Har Homa and the settlements will continue.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to send Abu Mazen and Saeb Erekat to the United States; there could be a working Israeli-Palestinian meeting this week.
- Jewish Federation in the United States transfers United Jewish Appeal donations to Reform and Conservative movements in Israel.
- Three Givati soldiers who beat Arabs with rifle butts and forced them to sing to be court-martialled.
- Pharmaceutical competition heats up: Four companies widen their activities in Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH

- U.S. programme to save peace: "(1) Arafat will fight terrorism, (2) Jewish settlement building to stop, (3) Generous second withdrawal from West Bank and (4) Acceleration of final-status negotiations".
MAARIV
- Clinton formulates "package deal" to accelerate final-status negotiations. Netanyahu at end of the White House meeting: No pressures, no threats.
